newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. anti-drug chief to visit Colombia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. anti-drug chief to visit Colombia.

text.p: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration chief Thomas Constantine will visit Colombia for the first time next week, officials said on Thursday.
Colombia's National Police, which heads the fight against drugs, said the DEA director will spend less than a day in the in the cocaine-producing country.
Constantine is due to arrive on Tuesday and will meet with police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano and the head of the police's anti-narcotics division, Col. Leonardo Gallego.

He may also meet with Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri but not with President Ernesto Samper, whom U.S. anti-drug officials consider corrupt for allegedly using drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
Colombia's Congress is about to reopen debate on a bill to lift a six-year-old ban on extraditing Colombian citizens to stand trial abroad.
In March, Washington blacklisted or "decertified" Colombia for a second consecutive year for failing to crack down hard enough on drug trafficking.
The DEA estimates Colombia still provides about 80 percent of the world's cocaine supply and has become the main supplier of high-grade heroin to the United States.
